transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been taking on too much. I keep starting things—work plans, certification schedules, stuff at home like network upgrades, even messaging old contacts. It gets hard to stop, and it kind of runs past what’s reasonable until my wife or my director has to step in.
During these times, do you also feel unusually up, euphoric, or unusually irritable compared with your normal self?

Yeah… during those weeks I can feel kind of wired. Like, really up, like I can push through anything. But I also get irritated fast. If something slows me down, or my wife asks a question, I can snap at it like it’s on purpose.
During those times, do you need much less sleep than usual?
Yeah. I mean… there are stretches where I’ll sleep maybe three hours and wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning, and I don’t feel tired. It feels more like I got extra time somehow.
During those wired, up periods, have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or believed things that others said weren’t true?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like saying it that way, but during the really driven stretches, when I’m barely sleeping, I’ve heard… like comments in the server noise. And I’ve read work messages like there were hidden threats in them, even when other people said that wasn’t there.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in almost everything?
Yeah… I think so. There are stretches where I wake up just feeling like… a failed version of myself. Heavy. Flat. Even my wife asking normal questions feels like too much to deal with.
During one of those wired, up periods, were you ever hospitalized because of it?
No… I don’t think I was ever hospitalized for that. It got bad, but not… not to that point.
Have you ever heard those comments or felt those hidden threats at a time when you were not in one of those wired, up periods?

Yeah… not as often, but yes. There were times when I wasn’t really wired or especially depressed—just kind of calm or flat—and I’d still think Teams statuses were… like coded warnings. And I’d hear brief comments when nobody was there. Sometimes for a few weeks.
Have there ever been two full weeks when you were hearing those comments or thinking messages had hidden warnings while you were not feeling especially up, irritable, or depressed?

Yeah… I think so. There were a few stretches like that, maybe a few weeks, where I wasn’t really up or depressed. Just kind of flat. But I still thought the Teams statuses meant something… like warnings. And I’d hear little comments when nobody was there.
Looking across the whole time this has been happening, have those warning-type thoughts or heard comments been present for most of the time you’ve been ill?
Yeah… I guess so. It’s been going on, off and on, for maybe a year and a half. Not every single day, but… a lot of that time.
